title: Clover Benchmark Inventory and Results
p: The strongest direct Office comparison covers 50 matched WorkBuddy tasks. Clover averaged 74.44% on deterministic checks and Qwen3.6-Flash averaged 72.14%. Browser, coding, reasoning, data generation, and speed results span different checkpoints and evaluation setups. Each result below names the setup needed to interpret it.

These evaluations cover completing tasks on realistic sites or small browser widgets. WorkBuddy Web, WebArena and MiniWoB++ are public suites. WindTunnel is a public benchmark from the nekuda-ai project, with local DiffuSpace runs and recorded races.

Clover rolled out all 70 public Web v1.0 tasks with CodeBuddy. The earlier run preserved 13 workspaces and produced six resolved deferred scores and seven ranges. The serial run preserved 70 workspaces. Deferred Luna grading and browser replay yielded a conservative 26.14% mean, with bounds of 26.14% to 36.86%. The final record has 51 resolved task scores and 19 ranges. The native Web verifier emitted no final rewards, and there is no paired scored comparator.

Terminal-Bench tests an agent in a command-line environment. SWE-bench tests repository fixes. LiveCodeBench and SciCode evaluate standalone coding. The launch runs use different benchmark versions and harnesses from our three-task Terminal-Bench 4.1.0 pilot.

The public pilot selected music-harmony, layout-config-recreation and vf2-speedup-networkx. Clover with mini-swe-agent hit context limits on all three and produced no valid score. Serial request compaction cleared those errors but the agents looped and were interrupted before grading. Pi with ARM verifiers scored reward 0 on all three at both 8K and 32K output caps. Local MiniCPM-V 4.7 Q4_K_M with Pi likewise scored 0 on all three at 32K. Clover repeated tool calls or exhausted its cap on two tasks. MiniCPM had no consecutive identical tool actions and stayed below the cap.

Earlier hosted diffusion checkpoint. Approx. 410, 280 and 210 decode tokens/s per request at concurrency 1, 4 and 10. Aggregate throughput rose from about 335 to 1,550 tokens/s, with time to first token near 0.85 s. Code reached 706 and prose 270–310 at concurrency one.

At one request, Clover Q4_K_M AR 61.8 tokens/s, Qwen3.6 GGUF 65.1, Qwen3.6 NVFP4 + MTP 105.5 and MiniCPM-V 4.7 78. At 32, Clover 204 aggregate, Qwen GGUF 235 and Qwen MTP 630.
Launch agent replay and edge speed

Launch materials report Clover 680 overall tokens/s on GB300 internal agent replay and 515 on H200 vs Qwen3.6 DFlash2 365. On RTX 5070 Ti, launch INT4 Clover reached 101.8 tokens/s on public MATH-500, with a 48.5-token/s comparison cited for similar-size models.

The original public GGUF failed to load in the tested local runtime. A fresh conversion of the BF16 Preview weights with the in-house converter produced an 853-tensor GGUF and passed a short GPU smoke. Initial warm trials were slower with self-speculation. Repetition and stopping tests found that verifier expert count and acceptance policy materially changed outcomes. A repeated 128K manual workload reached 185.88 self-speculative vs 68.46 AR decode tokens/s, with repetitive answers in both arms.

PR #4 default penalized Q4_K_M measured 58.22 self vs 75.43 AR pooled decode tokens/s on five varied prompts. The short structured panel achieved 122.89 vs 77.69 with threshold acceptance. The exact verifier reproduced all 20 AR answers byte for byte and both passed 16/20 checks. Across two orders, exact self achieved 67.09 vs 53.09 including prefill and HTTP.

The Q4_0 long-form finalist averaged 84.35 pooled decode tokens/s across two passes vs 65.01 for full-history AR. Each utility passed 4/5 checks, and the blinded rubric scored self 8.9/10 vs AR 9.7/10. In a five-workload follow-up, self/AR decode rates were 81.02/79.50 for handbook, 74.69/80.82 for novella, 100.15/76.90 for catalog, 111.15/73.71 for chaptered novella and 151.66/68.76 for manifest. The self chaptered novella repeated and the manifests had 492/560 vs 560/560 correct records. Both missed the outer array. DeepTutor chat and cache probes verified local integration and prefix reuse under particular prompt layouts.

td.p: Synthetic dependency density, internal exact-output tasks
DiffusionGemma 9/9 at 32 values, 6/6 at 48, 4/6 at 56. The tested 64-value controls produced no exact pass. Partial business screen 6/21 exact-valid with 8 budget exhaustions.
DiffusionGemma runtime repairs
Native stop, softcap and prompt-budget diagnostics. Incremental prefill lowered wall time 34% on three cases. Nine formerly capped cases reached native EOG with a larger allowance.
Nemotron-3B decoding candidates
Linear speculation matched its own AR output in the candidate screen with 4.9–7.3× lower batch-1 latency. Plain diffusion duplicated adjacent tokens and failed exact outputs.
Homework grading and path planning, internal

Nemotron-3B AR, linear and diffusion scored 213/300, 213/300 and 158/300 on the 50-item grading sheets, and 11/20, 11/20 and 4/20 valid on easy grids. Nemotron-14B scored 121/300, 118/300 and 173/300 on the 50-item sheets, and 6/60, 6/60 and 3/60 valid on hard grids.
Gemma homework and planning smoke
Gemma 4 AR without thinking vs DiffusionGemma, 4/5 vs 3/5 valid grids and 35/35 for both on homework. Thinking-on AR hit all seven output caps.
LLM-JEPA on Nemotron-3B, public prescription datasets
Diffusion exact match on NL-RX-SYNTH 44.5 baseline, 36.2 bidirectional JEPA, 47.2 causal JEPA. NL-RX-TURK 28.9, 16.9 and 21.8. Diffusion content accuracy fell 6.5–10.4 points under JEPA.
Legacy Colab and lab demos

Schedule puzzle, terminal runner, diffusion optimization and microbench. One archived terminal-runner example reported 2.16× lower median latency for DiffusionGemma. The archive records configuration and limitations.
